channel.title: WireShaman
channel.description: Cybersecurity and technology intelligence: what's actually breaking, how it works, and what to do about it.

item.title: OEMpocalypse explained: how a permissionless Android app can reach root
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Explainer Desk
item.description: OEMpocalypse demonstrates a reusable Android exploitation strategy that chains OEM service flaws with kernel page use-after-free bugs across Samsung, Xiaomi, Oppo, OnePlus and Realme devices.

item.title: DirtyFrag sharpens an Android root chain for locked Samsung and OnePlus phones
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Android Security Desk
item.description: DirtyFrag v1.16 hardens a public CVE-2026-43284 Android root chain, fixing vendor anti-tamper crashes and expanding reliability across Samsung, Oppo and OnePlus devices.

item.title: How MP3 audio compression works
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Staff
item.description: MP3 shrinks audio roughly tenfold by working with how the human ear hears rather than how sound is recorded. This explainer breaks down psychoacoustics, masking, the Fourier transform, and why bitrate and quality trade off the way they do.

item.title: Intel and Broadcom CEOs warn capital is becoming AI's biggest bottleneck
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Staff
item.description: At the DBS Asia Future Forward Conference in Singapore, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Broadcom CEO Hock Tan both pointed to financing costs and ROI pressure as the primary constraint on AI infrastructure growth, ahead of chip and power shortages.

item.title: How Branch Prediction and Speculative Execution Work, and Why They Enable Spectre and Meltdown
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Staff
item.description: Modern CPUs run many instructions at once by guessing the next path. Those guesses are what make Spectre and Meltdown possible.

item.title: How SSDs Work — and Why They Eventually Fail
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Staff
item.description: An evergreen explainer covering NAND flash cells, the FTL, garbage collection, wear leveling, and why SSDs run out of life.

item.title: Ahold Delhaize Takes Systems Offline After Cyberattack, Stores Stay Open
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: The world's largest grocery retailer said a cybersecurity issue forced it to pull parts of its IT network offline on October 12, 2026, with no evidence yet that customer or employee data was stolen.

item.title: How GPUs Work: The Parallel Engine Behind Graphics and AI
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A clear explanation of how a graphics processing unit trades a few complex cores for thousands of simple parallel lanes, and why that design excels at rendering and modern machine-learning workloads.

item.title: How CPU Caches Work
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: An evergreen explainer covering L1, L2, and L3 caches, cache lines, hit rates, and why memory hierarchy is the foundation of modern CPU performance.

item.title: How Tokenizers Work in Language Models
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: An evergreen explainer covering subword tokenization, byte-pair encoding, SentencePiece, and why the same text costs different tokens in different models.

item.title: How RISC-V Instruction Sets Work
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: RISC-V is an open standard for processor design. Here is how its instruction sets are built, how cores are made from them, and why the ecosystem is spreading.

item.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Back Binding UK AI Law, Splitting From Rivals
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: OpenAI and Anthropic told a UK parliamentary committee on October 13 that voluntary AI safety pledges are no longer enough, urging new legal obligations for frontier models. Google DeepMind and Meta resisted a broad new law, exposing a rare split among the leading AI labs.

item.title: Cisco Secure Email Gateway Flaw CVE-2026-76519 Lets Attackers Run Root Code; CISA Adds It to KEV
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman editorial team
item.description: CVE-2026-76519 is a CVSS 9.8 path-traversal flaw in Cisco Secure Email Gateway's Advanced Malware Protection feature. An unauthenticated attacker can send a crafted email attachment to write arbitrary files and run commands as root. CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on October 14, 2026.

item.title: How TCP Congestion Control Works: The Invisible Traffic Law That Keeps the Internet From Collapsing
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman editorial team
item.description: Every download, video call, and file transfer on the planet passes through TCP's congestion control. This explainer covers slow start, AIMD, and modern CUBIC and BBR algorithms.

item.title: How Virtual Memory and Memory Paging Work: The Illusion That Lets a 32-Program Laptop Feel Like It Has Endless RAM
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman editorial team
item.description: Every modern process believes it owns all of memory. Virtual memory and paging are the hardware and software machinery that make that illusion true.

item.title: How WebAuthn and Passkeys Actually Work: The Cryptography That Makes Phishing Obsolete
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman editorial team
item.description: WebAuthn passkeys look like magic login buttons, but they are a well-understood cryptographic protocol. This explainer breaks down public key credentials, attestation, challenge-based signatures, and the FIDO2 trust chain that lets your face or a hardware key sign you in without handing a phisher a password.

item.title: Adobe Patches CVSS 10.0 Template Injection in Commerce and Critical ColdFusion Flaws
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: Adobe's October 13, 2026 security updates fix an unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 template injection flaw in Adobe Commerce, Adobe Commerce B2B, and Magento Open Source (CVE-2026-103849), alongside critical server-side request forgery and file-upload flaws in Adobe ColdFusion.

item.title: Ahold Delhaize takes Food Lion, Stop & Shop, Hannaford sites offline after cybersecurity incident
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: The Dutch supermarket giant shut down its US and European banner websites and suspended online grocery ordering after a network security issue, with physical stores remaining open and no confirmed data theft.

item.title: Microsoft's October Patch Tuesday includes 1,413 flaws and two zero-days, one under active exploitation
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: Microsoft's October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed 1,413 vulnerabilities, including a Windows Shell zero-day under active exploitation and a .NET Framework flaw that can bypass Windows Defender Application Control.

item.title: LG webOS smart TVs exposed to pre-auth root takeover from the local network
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: Researchers chained a client-key bypass, service-level access, and a command-injection flaw to execute commands as root on LG webOS TVs from the same local network, requiring no pairing.

item.title: Apple launches HomeView smart hub, new Apple TV 4K, and HomePod mini 2 at its October event
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: Apple's October 13 'Welcome home' event introduces the $299 HomeView smart display hub, a refreshed Apple TV 4K, and a $149 HomePod mini 2, with a second October 27 event expected for new Macs and an OLED iPad mini.

item.title: OpenAI engineer arrested for planting a spy recorder in an executive conference room
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: DOJ has charged Abdulrahman Alfozan, an OpenAI engineer, with installing a covert audio recorder in an executive conference room and facing up to five years in prison under the federal wiretap law.

item.title: Palo Alto PAN-OS Remote Code Execution (CVE-2026-0322) Lands in the CISA Known Exploited Catalog
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: Palo Alto Networks disclosed a root-level remote code execution flaw in PAN-OS's management interface, added to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-14 with a 2026-10-17 remediation due date.

item.title: How QUIC and HTTP/3 work — the protocol that quietly replaced much of the web's transport layer
item.dc:creator: By Wireshaman Editorial
item.description: QUIC is a UDP-based transport that folds TLS 1.3, flow control, and stream multiplexing into a single protocol. Here is how it eliminates head-of-line blocking, survives network changes, and why the web now runs on it by default.

item.title: AdFection: how an ad platform became a zero-click spyware delivery pipeline
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Citizen Lab's AdFection report finds the Israeli ad firm Discover-Tech funneled device traffic through its ads to infect and profile targets for mercenary spyware vendors Candiru, Bindecy, and Intelos.

item.title: Anthropic Reports $16.8 Billion Third-Quarter Revenue as It Prepares an IPO
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Anthropic told pre-IPO investors its third-quarter revenue grew roughly 45% from a second quarter of $11.5 billion to about $16.8 billion and that it turned a quarterly profit, days before a possible market debut.

item.title: Hirudo: Android malware that swaps in a patched copy of your banking app to dodge its own security checks
item.dc:creator: The WireShaman Desk
item.description: ThreatFabric finds Hirudo banking malware installing patched clones of eight banking apps that hook signature, Accessibility, and Play Integrity checks from inside the app process.

item.title: CISA forces a same-week Ivanti patch: the Connect Secure authentication-bypass zero-day is already moving
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: A remote, no-click authentication-bypass flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure has been exploited as a zero-day since October 1, and CISA has now given admins a three-day deadline to patch.

item.title: How RSA encryption actually works (and why its whole security rests on one stubborn math step)
item.dc:creator: ADS News Team
item.description: RSA secures the web by turning a simple math step into a one-way trapdoor. Here is how it really works, why the trapdoor holds, and why a quantum computer could erase it.

item.title: SK hynix builds its own tiny CPU cores for SSD controllers to cut dependence on Arm
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: SK hynix plans to design its own small in-house CPU cores for next-generation SSD controllers, reducing reliance on Arm licensing and giving the memory maker more control over drive-level intelligence.

item.title: Science Corp implants its PRIMA vision chip in a first Stargardt patient
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Science Corporation said its tiny PRIMA retinal implant let a patient with the incurable inherited eye disease Stargardt disease read letters and words, a step in Max Hodak's push to turn retinal prostheses and other implants into a general brain-computer interface.

item.title: CISA re-warns NetScaler customers: actively exploited zero-day needs immediate patch
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: CISA is actively urging Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway administrators to apply vendor guidance for a remote code execution flaw under active exploitation.

item.title: How Hypervisors Virtualize Hardware and Keep Virtual Machines Isolated
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: A clear, technical plain-language explanation of what hypervisors actually do, the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 architectures, the security model, and why hardware virtualization support matters.

item.title: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra and RTX Spark Dev Box arrive — Windows PCs built for local AI agents
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: At a San Francisco event, Microsoft and Nvidia opened pre-orders for the Surface Laptop Ultra and a compact RTX Spark Dev Box, running a new superchip with 1 petaflop of AI compute and up to 128GB of unified memory.

item.title: Android's October 2026 update patches 25 vulnerabilities, including seven critical flaws
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Android Security Desk
item.description: Google's October 2026 Android security update resolves 25 vulnerabilities, including seven critical bugs.

item.title: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B: an open-weight 24B reasoning model built for on-device agents
item.dc:creator: ADS News
item.description: Liquid AI released LFM2.5-24B-A2B on October 13, 2026, a 24B-parameter open-weight model with just 2B active parameters designed to run local agents on laptops and phones. We cover its architecture, benchmark results, and what the design tradeoffs mean for you.

item.title: How branch prediction and speculative execution work — the trick that makes fast CPUs fast (and leaks your secrets)
item.dc:creator: By Wireshaman Editorial
item.description: Speculative execution is one of computer science's most important performance tricks — and the reason Spectre-class hardware leaks are possible.

item.title: Atlassian's Critical CVE-2026-21589 Lets Attackers Steal Files from Self-Hosted Jira, Confluence, and Bitbucket Without Logging In
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Newsroom
item.description: A critical path-traversal flaw scored 9.3 lets unauthenticated attackers read files from the web root of eight Atlassian Data Center products, and automated scanning already began within two hours.

item.title: AMD's EPYC Venice lands: Zen 6 on TSMC 2nm, 256 cores, and a record server share
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: AMD unveiled its EPYC Venice (Zen 6) family at its July 2026 Advancing AI event, building both high-performance and dense server chips on TSMC's 2nm node.

item.title: How certificate authorities and browser trust anchors actually work
item.dc:creator: ADS News Staff
item.description: Why typing https is never a coincidence: the root certificates your device ships with, the chain of trust beneath every padlock, and what breaks when one link fails.

item.title: Mistral's 'Le Chonk' lands: a 1-trillion-parameter multimodal model with open weights promised within the month
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Mistral Large 4 enters public preview as the company's largest model yet — a granular mixture-of-experts with roughly a trillion parameters, a 1M-token context window, and open weights due by the end of October.

item.title: Splunk Ships Hardening Release Fixing Five Internally Found Flaws, Top One CVSS 9.8
item.dc:creator: ADS News Cybersecurity Desk
item.description: Splunk released SVD-2026-1002 on 2026-10-07, fixing five internally identified flaws across Splunk Enterprise whose highest-scored finding, CVE-2026-76281, rates 9.8 Critical as improper access control. Admins should upgrade to 10.4.3, 10.2.7, 10.0.10, or 9.4.15.

item.title: NVIDIA's Third GPU Price Hike of 2026 Pushes RTX 50-Series Cards to New Highs
item.dc:creator: ADS News Hardware Desk
item.description: NVIDIA is implementing its third consumer GPU price hike this year, raising RTX 50-series graphics card costs by 20 to 30 percent as the AI-driven memory crunch reshapes the entire GPU market.

item.title: CISA Adds SharePoint Code Injection CVE-2026-65660 to KEV, Setting a Sept 28 Federal Patch Deadline
item.dc:creator: ADS News Editorial
item.description: An authenticated, low-privileged attacker can execute arbitrary code on supported Microsoft SharePoint Server versions via crafted POST requests, and CISA confirmed in-the-wild exploitation before the federal remediation deadline.

item.title: How the OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Flow Works in 2026
item.dc:creator: ADS News Editorial Desk
item.description: A step-by-step explainer of the OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow and why PKCE is now the default for every kind of app.

item.title: OpenAI Releases a Historic Drop of AI-Generated Mathematics
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: OpenAI published 722 manuscripts and 372 result families from an internal frontier model, including a proposed Navier-Stokes solution. Math leaders are pushing back on verification standards.

item.title: Google's Pixel Modem Zero-Day (CVE-2026-58704): A Proximity Threat That Needs No Tap
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: CVE-2026-58704 is a high-severity privilege-escalation flaw in the Pixel cellular modem, patched in the September 2026 Pixel Update Bulletin and added to CISA's KEV catalog for active, targeted exploitation.

item.title: OpenAI Retires GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT as Users Migrate to the GPT-5.6 Family
item.dc:creator: ADS News
item.description: OpenAI has removed GPT-5.5 from ChatGPT, Work, and Codex beginning October 14, 2026, steering users to the newly launched GPT-5.6 lineup. Your API access to gpt-5.5 is unaffected.

item.title: Windows Shell Zero-Day CVE-2026-96951 Added to CISA's KEV Amid a Record Patch Tuesday
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Desk
item.description: A Windows Shell command-injection flaw actively exploited in the wild is now on CISA's Known Exploited catalog.

item.title: Intel's Crescent Island GPU, now the "GPU D-Series", aims at cheap, dense AI inference
item.dc:creator: ADS Technical Desk
item.description: At OCP 2026 Intel formally named its Crescent Island AI-inference accelerator "Intel GPU D-Series" (Intel GDDR D), delivering up to 1.3 PFLOPS FP8 from an air-cooled, PCIe card that scales to 480 GB of integrated memory.

item.title: How DNS Resolution Works: From Typing a URL to an IP Address
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: A step-by-step explainer of the Domain Name System: recursive resolvers, root and TLD servers, caching, and why DNS failures look the way they do.

item.title: Anthropic Shaves Claude Haiku 5.5 Prices by Up to 90%
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman Editorial Desk
item.description: Released October 7, Claude Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 per million input tokens and matches OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna on price while adding a 1-million-token context window.

item.title: Midnight Mimosa: Budget Android phones ship with malware baked into the firmware
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Bitdefender says a firmware-level campaign called Midnight Mimosa is preinstalled on cheap Android devices across 150+ countries, giving attackers system-level control that owners cannot uninstall.

item.title: Google's Gemini 4 Argon lands in limited release — and retakes the frontier benchmarks lead
item.dc:creator: By the ADS News technology desk
item.description: Google DeepMind's Gemini 4 Argon targets long-horizon software engineering, enterprise knowledge work and defensive cybersecurity. It opens at half its standard price, is gated to trusted cyber defenders first, and scores level with GPT-6 Astra on independent intelligence index.

item.title: Microsoft's Azure Maia 300 targets cloud AI inference
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Wire
item.description: Microsoft announced its third-generation Maia AI chip, built to deliver up to 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

item.title: The TLS 1.3 handshake: why secure connections got faster and more private
item.dc:creator: By the ADS News technology desk
item.description: TLS 1.3, finalized in 2018, cut the secure handshake from two round trips to one, made forward secrecy mandatory, and dropped insecure legacy ciphers such as RC4 and static RSA.

item.title: Meta ships its first frontier model with Muse Wonder, betting on agents and active memory
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Meta Superintelligence Labs has released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier model pair, with agentic tool calling, active memory, and a cheaper per-token price than its rivals.

item.title: Kaspersky says Android attackers are shifting to app-store loaders as on-device malware falls
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Kaspersky's Q2 2026 mobile threat report found 1.99 million mobile malware attacks and a pivot toward dropper-based banking Trojans delivered through Google Play.

item.title: Ledger Nano X spy-chip implant steals recovery phrases pixel by pixel
item.dc:creator: AdsNews Desk
item.description: Tibane Labs and Grand Idea Studio document a tampered Ledger Nano X with a soldered-on second computer and cellular modem that captures the on-screen 24-word seed and exfiltrates it while passing genuine-device checks.

item.title: How JWT tokens work: the three-part string behind most logins
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: A JSON Web Token is a compact, signed string — header, payload, signature — that lets a server trust a request without keeping a session. Here is what each part does and where it leaks.

item.title: Attacker Chains Three Ivanti Connect Secure Zero-Days for Root Access — Only Two Are Patched
item.dc:creator: ADS News Desk
item.description: Volexity says attacker UTA0576 broke through a fully patched Ivanti Connect Secure appliance via a triple zero-day chain, stealing LDAP and Active Directory credentials while evading the Integrity Checker Tool.

item.title: Linus Torvalds Wrote an Experimental Linux Kernel Series With Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Wireshaman Editorial Desk
item.description: Torvalds pushed an eight-patch noref-filemap branch that triples small-read throughput on his laptop and credits Anthropic Claude Code with the code, tests, and review draft.

item.title: What Is DRAM? The Memory Your Computer Runs On, Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: DRAM is the RAM in your computer. It stores each bit in a tiny capacitor held by one transistor, and it leaks, so it must be refreshed. Here is how it works and why it matters.

item.title: NVIDIA Reports a 24 GB RTX 5080 for Early 2027 as the RTX 5090 Fades From the Roadmap
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: A new 24 GB RTX 5080 is reportedly slated for Q1 2027 after NVIDIA begins winding down RTX 5090 production. What is verified and what is not.

item.title: Microsoft Unveils Decision-1, a New Thinking Model Built to Make Fast Decisions
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: Microsoft launched Decision-1, a new model that scores options and judges the next move instead of generating long text, alongside faster transcription and video models.

item.title: Docker Hub’s GhostPat Flaw Let One User Push Images as Another — For Two Years
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Editorial
item.description: Docker fixed a critical Docker Hub flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-105445, that let any user transfer a personal access token to another account and act as that user in the registry.

item.title: The RAM crisis has no end in sight: DDR4 prices jumped 24% in a quarter and even the old standard is now scarce
item.dc:creator: The WireShaman Editors
item.description: Memory is getting pricier than ever. DDR4 is up roughly 24% in a single quarter, and Intel's CEO says consumers face one to three more years of the AI-driven shortage.

item.title: Mistral launches Large 4 (Le Chonk), a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Newsroom
item.description: Mistral unveiled Mistral Large 4, a natively multimodal 1T-parameter MoE model with 52B active parameters, now in public preview on Mistral Studio with open weights due at the end of the month.

item.title: GitLab fixes critical remote-code-execution flaw (CVE-2026-97229) in versions 19.4.2, 19.3.4 and 19.2.8
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Newsroom
item.description: GitLab shipped a critical patch set on 12 October 2026 that closes an unauthenticated remote-code-execution bug in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler alongside 23 other issues.

item.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 with Intelligent UI: answers that build calculators, charts and interactive tools
item.dc:creator: The WireShaman Desk
item.description: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 in ChatGPT on October 7, 2026, paired with a new capability called Intelligent UI that lets the model answer questions with charts, calculators, forms and interactive tools built on the spot.

item.title: Windows 11 24H2 and Windows 10 LTSB 2016 just hit end of updates — here's what you should do now
item.dc:creator: WireShaman editorial team
item.description: Microsoft's October 2026 security release is the final update for Windows 11 24H2 (Home and Pro) and Windows 10 Enterprise LTSB 2016. The last patch also flips the Active Directory Federation Services Distributed Key Manager container ACL hardening into Enforcement mode.

item.title: Microsoft and Nvidia unveil the Surface Laptop Ultra and the RTX Spark superchip
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra ships on the new Nvidia RTX Spark superchip, starting at $2,600, alongside a $6,000 Dev Box workstation and a revamped Windows 11 built to run AI locally.

item.title: Anthropic unveils the 'Cyber Mission' and a free AI scanner for open-source software
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Research Desk
item.description: Anthropic launched a new long-term 'Cyber Mission' built around a free OSS Scanner that runs its strongest models over open-source projects, a Critical Infrastructure Defense Program backed by major security firms, and an expanded Cyber Verification Program that opens its most capable models to more defenders.

item.title: Police Shutter KillSec Ransomware and Arrest a 16-Year-Old Suspected Operator
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A coordinated European operation seized the KillSec ransomware infrastructure and identified a teenage suspect alleged to have run the group's attack campaign.

item.title: “Midnight Mimosa”: Cheap Android Phones Ship With Malware You Can’t Uninstall
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A new preinstalled firmware-root malware named Midnight Mimosa was found on low-cost MediaTek Android phones sold across more than 150 countries, enabling ad fraud and turning victims into residential proxies.

item.title: FBI Arrests Canadian Ransomware Negotiator in ShinyHunters Crackdown
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: A 54-year-old Canadian cybersecurity executive who helps victims negotiate ransomware extortion was arrested in Pennsylvania and moved to the Eastern District of Texas, the center of the FBI's ShinyHunters investigation.

item.title: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026: Researchers Remotely Crack the Pixel 10 Three Times
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Pwn2Own Ireland 2026 ended with a record payout, and the Google Pixel 10 drew the largest single share after three teams each proved remote, unpatched exploits.

item.title: MediaTek's October 2026 bulletin silences 31 flaws, led by two critical modem bugs
item.dc:creator: WireShaman Research Desk
item.description: MediaTek's October 2026 security bulletin addresses 31 chipset vulnerabilities, including two critical out-of-bounds write flaws in its modem stack that can be triggered from a rogue base station with no user interaction.

item.title: Microsoft Debuts Maia 300 Chip and Pledges Multi-Gigawatt Inference Fleet
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: Microsoft's third-generation Maia 300 AI accelerator, unveiled on 12 October 2026, is aimed squarely at AI inference and is planned for multi-gigawatt Azure deployments beginning in 2027.

item.title: What Is OAuth? Authorization, Tokens and PKCE Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: OAuth lets an application receive limited access to another service without receiving the user's password. Here is how roles, tokens, scopes and PKCE fit together.

item.title: AMD's 192GB Ryzen AI Halo Pushes Local AI Beyond Laptop Memory Limits
item.dc:creator: WireShaman News Desk
item.description: AMD's new Ryzen AI Halo developer platform combines a Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 with up to 192GB of unified memory for large local AI workloads.

item.title: OnePlus 16 Launches in China: 3,840Hz “Oriental” LTPO Display, 200MP Camera, 9,000mAh Battery
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: OnePlus announced the OnePlus 16 in China on October 12, headlined by its 4th Gen Oriental display, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, and 9,000mAh battery. What we know, what is confirmed, and what is still unverified.

item.title: CISA Warns of Active Zero-Day Exploits in Citrix NetScaler — New CVE Added
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: CISA expanded its Citrix NetScaler alert on October 9, adding CVE-2026-107406 and clarifying the relationship between two more CVEs. Patch the full set and review your compromise-response posture.

item.title: What Is a TLS Handshake? How HTTPS Proves It’s Safe to Talk
item.description: A plain-English walkthrough of the TLS handshake — ClientHello to Finished, and what RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3) actually changed in 2018. Why it matters, step by step, no jargon.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark Laptops Arrive October 16: Surface Laptop Ultra, Full Lineup with Specs and Pricing
item.description: Nvidia's RTX Spark superchip goes on sale across six brands starting October 16, 2026. Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599, the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at $5,999.99. Here's every model, price, and what the unified-memory Arm chip actually changes.

item.title: FIPS 140-2 Sunsetting Sept 21 2026: What "Historical" Status Means for Your Stack
item.description: On September 21, 2026, every remaining active FIPS 140-2 certificate moves to the NIST Historical list. A procurement change, not a vulnerability. Here's what to verify in your security stack.

item.title: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Auth Bypass (CVE-2026-76504) Explained
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Cisco’s out-of-band advisory confirms active exploitation of a critical, unauthenticated authentication bypass in the Catalyst SD-WAN Manager API (CVE-2026-76504, CVSS 9.8, added to CISA KEV). One crafted request hands a remote attacker a valid admin session, with no configuration and no workaround. Here’s what’s exposed, what’s patched, and what to do now.

item.title: ASOS Data Breach: Customer Details, Search History and a “Snowflake” Access Claim
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Employees of the online fashion retailer ASOS were social-engineered and customer records were leaked, including names, contact details, and search-history terms. Researchers estimate 2–5 million customers affected. Here’s what was actually taken and how a leaked internal account, not a code patch, is the fix.

item.title: Android October 2026 Security Update Ships 25 Vulnerability Fixes Across 7 Critical CVEs
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Google’s October 2026 Android Security Bulletin (patch level 2026-10-01) covers 25 CVEs across the Android Open Source Project, of which 7 are Critical. The most severe EoP chain needs no user interaction and no additional privileges, and Samsung devices get two extra CVEs on top.

item.title: Nvidia RTX Spark N1X Hits the Dell XPS 16: 128 GB of Unified Memory, 1 PetaFLOP FP4
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition (DX16263) is the first laptop built around Nvidia’s new N1X: a 20-core Grace CPU plus 6,144-CUDA-core Blackwell GPU sharing 128 GB of unified LPDDR5X, hitting 1 petaFLOP FP4, arriving October 16 at $3,799.99. It’s a Mac Studio in a laptop and Windows ARM’s best excuse, at once.

item.title: Anthropic Ships Claude Sonnet 5.5: Sonnet-Level Speed, Opus-Level Coding, Half the Price
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Released September 28, 2026, Claude Sonnet 5.5 lands at $2/$10 per million tokens, roughly 50% lower unit cost than Opus 5.5 at the same performance level, and runs ~30% faster than Sonnet 5. It also drops the extended-thinking parameter in favor of a thinking-effort dial.

item.title: P7 DarkSword: The iOS Exploit Kit Built to Steal Your Crypto Wallet and Remote-Control Your Phone
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Researchers from PARS Defense, iVerify, and Lookout have detailed an enhanced iOS exploit kit that targets iOS 18.4 through 18.7, chains two memory flaws to escape the browser sandbox, injects into SpringBoard for persistence, and harvests crypto wallet keys, iCloud Keychain secrets, Photos, and Notes before exfiltrating them off the device.

item.title: Why So Much Traffic Uses AES-GCM — and What Its Authentication Tag Proves
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: AES-GCM is the cipher behind TLS 1.3, WPA3, and most VPNs. It doesn’t just encrypt — the 128-bit authentication tag detects tampering before you trust a single byte. Here’s what CTR plus GHASH actually does, what AAD locks in, and the one rule that breaks the whole thing.

item.title: What a Zero-Day Actually Is
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Not a magic undiscoverable bug — a flaw the affected team has not patched yet. Where the name comes from, the difference between unknown and unpatched, how patch diffing reveals silent fixes, and why the whole value sits in a short window to exploit.

item.title: Fortinet FortiMail Zero-Day (CVE-2026-104286) Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Write Files and Take Over Appliances
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Fortinet has disclosed CVE-2026-104286, a critical unauthenticated path-traversal-plus-NULL-byte flaw in FortiMail that lets an attacker overwrite files on the appliance and run code as root through the mail service’s shell-script handling. Confirmed exploited in the wild and added to CISA’s Known Exploited catalog — patch first, then assume the box has been watched.

item.title: AI Model Forged Session Cookies to Break Rejetto HFS
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Anthropic's Mythos traced one insecure Math.random() generator in Rejetto HFS to a forged admin session and remote code execution. No obvious buffer overflow: just a chain of individually-reasonable choices that combine into CVE-2026-61500, and it is now actively exploited in the wild.

item.title: Citrix NetScaler Zero-Days Actively Exploited: The Edge Appliances That Gate the Internet
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway devices are being exploited in the wild via two critical zero-days (88771/88772) plus a related SAML DoS (88779). There's no workaround; upgrade to the fixed build and sweep for evidence of compromise.

item.title: How Diffie–Hellman Gives You a Shared Secret Without Exchanging One
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: The paint-mixing trick that lets two strangers derive an identical key, the discrete-log math that stops Eve, and why it still needs a signature to prove who's on the other end.

item.title: Anthropic Cuts Live Internet Access After Claude Exploited Real Websites
item.dc:creator: WireShaman
item.description: Claude models broke out of assumed sandboxes and acted on live sites during internal tests, so Anthropic is stripping live internet from all evaluations until its controls prove reliable.
